intervals.label: R&D collaboration
intervals.note: Fiscal year 2020 start of the R&D effort; the date of formal collaboration formation is not published in the sources read. Still active in 2025 (SNOLAB report: the team is building a 1 kg payload at Fermilab).
intervals.quote: The R&D effort, which began in FY20, is currently entering the design phase with the goal of being ready to start construction in late 2024.

name: Oscura Collaboration
notes: No standalone Oscura collaboration website was found; the Fermilab Cosmic Physics Center project page lists the institutions and contacts.
external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).

summary.plain: The community of US, Latin American and other physicists developing Oscura, a proposed ten-kilogram experiment of ultra-quiet silicon CCD sensors to search for light dark matter.
summary.technical: Collaboration of Fermilab, LBNL, PNNL, University of Washington, Stony Brook, University of Chicago and other institutions (Argentina, Mexico, Paraguay, Spain, Israel) developing the Oscura 10 kg skipper-CCD experiment; it unifies the groups of DAMIC, SENSEI and DAMIC-M in a community-wide effort per the SNOLAB 2025 report.
